answer: When lightning flashes, the claimant records the seconds between flash and thunder, and three nearby reports must triangulate the same strike the national lightning network logged. A prism of light splits the sky, ferrous railings hum after the bolt, and the ripple of thunder rolling across the valley gives the same distance from different porches. One person can only be at one distance from a strike, so a farm claiming many distances for one bolt contradicts the physics of sound.
